<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **8** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/system.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/system.json`, `packages/spec/src/system/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/i18n-standard.mdx`  _(via PLATFORM_LOCALES (symbol, a top-level const object), PLATFORM_LOCALE_READ_ALIASES (symbol, a top-level const object), PLATFORM_LOCALE_TAGS (symbol, a top-level const object), platformLocaleTagOf (symbol, a top-level function))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/system.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/system.json`, `packages/spec/src/system/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **61** of **219** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **158** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **158**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **103** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **169** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f19fbb8f2cb92fe3deb19a0dd8456ad49aeeb667` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `d2cb27b1fd7be9956a7106d7d141ce52fc012271` — the merge of head `a8e812094c6d07538541f1e6f734276516672223` into base `f19fbb8f2cb92fe3deb19a0dd8456ad49aeeb667`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin d2cb27b1fd7be9956a7106d7d141ce52fc012271 && git checkout d2cb27b1fd7be9956a7106d7d141ce52fc012271
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin f19fbb8f2cb92fe3deb19a0dd8456ad49aeeb667 a8e812094c6d07538541f1e6f734276516672223 && git checkout -B drift-repro f19fbb8f2cb92fe3deb19a0dd8456ad49aeeb667 && git merge --no-ff a8e812094c6d07538541f1e6f734276516672223

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f19fbb8f2cb92fe3deb19a0dd8456ad49aeeb667
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs f19fbb8f2cb92fe3deb19a0dd8456ad49aeeb667` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `8810e33cc897b065e2c0fabbf70143b163a125d4`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/system/index.ts, packages/spec/src/system/platform-locales.ts + packages/spec/src/system/platform-locales.test.ts, packages/spec/api-surface/system.json, packages/spec/export-origins/system.json, .changeset/30001-platform-locale-table.md, content/docs/protocol/kernel/i18n-standard.mdx; read on origin/main: packages/spec/src/system/i18n-resolver.ts (resolveBundleLocale, isDefaultLocale), packages/spec/src/system/translation.zod.ts (LocaleSchema, canonicalLocaleCase, LOCALE_TAG_SHAPE), packages/spec/src/marketplace/package-l10n.ts, packages/spec/src/system/email-template.zod.ts, packages/spec/declaration-map/system.json, packages/spec/package.json, scripts/check-spec-parsed-alias.mjs, scripts/check-i18n-bundles.mjs, packages/cli/src/commands/i18n/extract.ts, ui/packages/i18n/src/locales/ (pack set, rtl.ts), ui/packages/i18n/src/pickLocalized.ts, skills/objectstack-i18n/SKILL.md, skills/objectui/guides/i18n.md

### ① Derived judgments

- Exports: six new names (`PLATFORM_LOCALES`, `PLATFORM_LOCALE_TAGS`, `PLATFORM_LOCALE_READ_ALIASES`, `platformLocaleTagOf`, `PlatformLocale`, `PlatformLocaleTag`) land in `api-surface/system.json` and `export-origins/system.json` with the right kinds and origins. No other ledger is owed: `declaration-map/system.json` keys only Zod def names (sibling consts `PKG_CONVENTIONS`, `preferredLocaleFromHeader` are absent on main), `content/docs/references/` and `llms.txt` name no sibling helper const, and `check:spec-parsed-alias` guards `XParsed` aliases of Zod schemas, of which this module declares none. Consistent with the dev's `check:generated` 14/14.
- Table: exactly the 11 tags of #29428 in the ruling's order; labels match ruling F's table verbatim (`简体中文`, `繁體中文`, `Português (Brasil)`, `العربية`, …); `rtl` true on `ar` alone. Pinned whole in the test.
- Frozen-ness: deep. The array is frozen and every row is a frozen spread copy of the private `as const` source; `PLATFORM_LOCALE_TAGS` and the alias record are frozen. Pinned.
- `platformLocaleTagOf`: a lowercase-keyed `Map` built from tags plus aliases, so it is case-insensitive (BCP 47 §2.1.1; #29895 measures `zh-cn`/`ZH-CN` stored by `PATCH sys_user`), answers the table's canonical spelling, and answers `undefined` for an unknown code and for a non-string. It does not trim and does not accept `_`; that is right: the `sys_user.locale` door already refuses `zh_CN` with 400 (#29895), `LocaleSchema`'s shape refuses it, and Prime Directive #12 forbids a lenient alias in a consumer. `Map` keeps `constructor`/`__proto__` from reading `Object.prototype`. The internal fold does not duplicate `canonicalLocaleCase`, which `translation.zod.ts` keeps package-internal on purpose; nothing new is exported that folds.
- Test arithmetic checks: 4 + 13 + 41 = 58 cases, as the PR states.
- Should-fix (typing): `PLATFORM_LOCALE_READ_ALIASES` is `Readonly<Record<string, PlatformLocaleTag>>`, so a consumer indexing it directly with an unknown code gets a non-undefined type. A record typed on the ten literal keys (derive from an `as const` object) keeps the index honest; `platformLocaleTagOf` stays the safe door either way.

### ② Semver level

`Clause-②: yes (widening)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, `patch` is right. Every name is new and nothing is removed or narrowed. No Zod schema reads the table: `LocaleSchema`, `supportedLocales`, `TranslationBundle` keys and `EMAIL_TEMPLATE_FLOOR_LOCALE` are untouched, so no key, accepted value or metadata type is added and no schema starts refusing or accepting anything; a tag off the table parses exactly as before. `none` takes `patch` by the AGENTS.md rule. Both declaration lines sit in the PR body and the changeset body; `Check Changeset` is green on the head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- os-dev-report (comment 6621844028): every field present, head matches, tests/gates/api_writes recorded, `open_questions` empty.
- `Fixes #30001` present; the card's newest `Claim:` names `claude/project-thread-wyvtjy`, the PR head. Head repo is the base repo (not a fork). No governed surface in the file list; 306 changed lines.
- `Prior rulings read:` present with ADR hits.
- `Skills-docs:` follow-up owed is the right disposition (lane paused). Verified on main: SKILL.md line 36 `['en','zh-CN','ja-JP','es-ES']`, line 49 `en-US, zh-CN, pt-BR, en-GB`, line 206 `en, en-US, zh-CN, pt-BR`; objectui i18n.md lines 134 and 183 `en, zh-CN, ja-JP`. Should-fix: the line claims every spelling "is a table tag or a read alias"; `en-GB` at line 49 is neither. No skills line is false (those are app-level `supportedLocales` examples, which the table does not close), but the owed note should say so rather than overstate the alias cover.
- Should-fix (process): the PR carries no assignee while the card is assigned to `os-support-ai`; AGENTS.md has the executor mirror the card's assignee at pr_create. The owning seat sets it; no content change.
- Check-runs on the head: every completed run is `success` or `skipped`; the required contexts (`Type Check`, `Build Core`, `Lint` lanes, UI lanes) were still `in_progress` at review time, so landing still waits on green.

### ④ Design judgment

- Fit for phases 2–4: rows `{ tag, label, rtl }` serve the locale menu (phase 4) and replace the UI's own `RTL_LANGUAGES` for table languages; `PLATFORM_LOCALE_TAGS` is what `i18n:extract --locales` and `check-i18n-bundles.mjs` need to read; today's UI packs are keyed `zh.ts`/`pt.ts`, both covered by the aliases, so phase 2 can rekey through `platformLocaleTagOf` without a second map.
- No existing helper duplicates or statically contradicts the aliases: `resolveBundleLocale` (spec), `resolvePackageL10nField` (spec marketplace) and the UI `pickLocalized` all expand a bare language to "the first registered variant" of whatever keys a bundle has; none pins `zh` to `zh-CN`. Latent disagreement: once a bundle carries both `zh-Hans` and `zh-Hant`, `resolveBundleLocale(bundle, 'zh')` answers by key order while the table says `zh-Hans`. Should-fix: one sentence in the new docs section (TSDoc too) saying `platformLocaleTagOf` is an identity lookup that runs before the bundle ladder, which the page's next section (`Locale Fallback`: `pt-BR` falls back to `pt`) still performs. As written, "`pt` reads as `pt-BR`, no region fallback is guessed" sits directly above "`pt-BR` → `pt`" with nothing relating the two.
- Must-fix (docs accuracy): the new section and the module TSDoc state, in the present tense on a served protocol page, "Every language on it is complete on every surface: the Console UI, platform metadata and the built-in emails." On main today the Console ships 10 packs with no `zh-Hant`, platform metadata ships 4 locales (`en`, `zh-CN`, `ja-JP`, `es-ES` across 10 packages) and the built-in emails 4 with an `en-US` floor. Seven of the eleven are absent from metadata and emails, so the page advertises what the runtime does not deliver (Prime Directive #10 corollary). State it as the rule the table binds every surface to, with the backfill tracked under the parent, not as a fact of the platform now.
- Customer-facing text: no `.describe()`, refusal or message string carries an issue id; the ids sit in code comments and TSDoc provenance only, as the sibling modules do.

Reviewed-by: `session_01WGufzfgvGexKn9vLHsy89K`

## Contract review — delta (fix round 1)

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `a8e812094c6d07538541f1e6f734276516672223`
Local-runs: none
Scope: delta (commits ea8473ef7, a8e812094): packages/spec/src/system/platform-locales.ts, packages/spec/src/system/platform-locales.test.ts, packages/spec/api-surface/system.json, packages/spec/export-origins/system.json, .changeset/30001-platform-locale-table.md, content/docs/protocol/kernel/i18n-standard.mdx; read on origin/main: packages/spec/src/system/i18n-resolver.ts (resolveBundleLocale 394–419), packages/spec/src/system/email-template.zod.ts (EMAIL_TEMPLATE_FLOOR_LOCALE), packages/plugins/plugin-email/src/templates/auth-templates.ts, ui/packages/i18n/src/locales/ (pack set, registry.ts), packages/{platform-objects,plugins/*,services/*}/src/translations/index.ts (10 packages), packages/spec/package.json + tsconfig.json/tsconfig.test.json, tsconfig.base.json, skills/objectstack-i18n/SKILL.md, skills/objectui/guides/i18n.md, AGENTS.md rule 10 and line 647; proposed body /mnt/project-files/seat3-orders/30001-body-r1.md; PR 30007 state and comments; check-runs on the head.

### ① Derived judgments

- MUST-FIX (docs accuracy): closed. The mdx section and the module TSDoc now state the table as the rule the three surfaces are held to and name what each serves today, in a `warn` Callout (the component is already used at lines 11 and 73 of the same page). Every factual claim checks against main: Console packs are exactly `ar de en es fr ja ko pt ru zh` (ten, no `zh-Hant`; registry.ts 78–86); platform metadata is `en`, `zh-CN`, `ja-JP`, `es-ES` in all ten `translations/index.ts` files; the built-in emails are `en-US`, `zh-CN`, `ja-JP`, `es-ES` (auth-templates.ts, eight rows each) and `EMAIL_TEMPLATE_FLOOR_LOCALE = 'en-US'`. The TSDoc's "`en` or `en-US`" is right: metadata keys `en`, emails `en-US`. The same-PR follow rule is reworded to "every language its surface carries", which is the only form a surface missing seven languages can obey today; the convergence clause ("once backfilled, that is every language on the table") keeps the rule bound to the table. Not a weakened guarantee: nothing a consumer could rely on before this PR is withdrawn.
- SHOULD-FIX 1 (lookup vs ladder): closed in both places. The TSDoc's four steps (exact, case, base language, first variant) are resolveBundleLocale's lines 398–416 exactly, and the key-order claim is right by reading: `{ 'zh-Hant', 'zh-Hans' }` asked for `zh` or `zh-CN` fails steps 1–3 and step 4 returns the first key whose base is `zh`, so `zh-Hant`; reversed keys answer `zh-Hans`. No resolver change, as asked. Residual should-fix below on the mdx referent.
- SHOULD-FIX 2 (skills line): closed in body r1, which now says `en-GB` (SKILL.md:49) is neither a tag nor an alias and stays valid as an app-level example. Lines 36, 49, 206 and objectui 134, 183 re-verified on current main.
- SHOULD-FIX 3 (alias typing): closed. `PLATFORM_LOCALE_READ_ALIASES` is `Object.freeze({…} as const satisfies Record<string, PlatformLocaleTag>)`, `PlatformLocaleReadAlias = keyof typeof …` is the ten-key union, and the test pins both directions (`'zh-Hans'` from `['zh-CN']`, `@ts-expect-error` on `['pt-PT']`). The expect-error is real under the test program: tsconfig.test.json inherits `strict: true` from tsconfig.base.json, so the unlisted index is TS7053; `check:test-typecheck` is part of `typecheck` (package.json 320–323) and every Type Check lane is green on the head. The `Object.entries(...) as Array<[string, PlatformLocaleTag]>` cast in the index builder is harmless (entries of the const object already carry the tag union).
- Ledgers: `PlatformLocaleReadAlias (type)` lands in api-surface/system.json and export-origins/system.json in the sibling form of `PlatformLocaleTag (type)`. No other ledger is owed (declaration-map keys Zod defs only; CHANGELOG is release-owned per AGENTS.md:647). Seven names in all, as the body says.
- Tests: 59 = 8 `it` + `it.each` rows 10 + 11 + 8 + 9 + 8 + 5; the body's "59 passed" is right.
- Should-fix (body wording): "the four value exports and the function are re-exported by the `system` barrel" reads as five; the barrel test checks three consts and the function. Say "the three value exports and the function".

### ② Semver level

`Clause-②: yes (widening)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, `patch` still holds. Every name is new against main (the alias record's narrower key type is a change inside this PR, not against any published shape), no Zod schema reads the table, `LocaleSchema`, `supportedLocales`, `EMAIL_TEMPLATE_FLOOR_LOCALE` and the resolver are untouched, so nothing starts refusing or accepting a value. Both declaration lines sit in the changeset and in body r1; `Check Changeset` is green.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Check-runs on the head: 65 runs, every one `completed`, each `success` or `skipped`; none in progress. PR 30007 head is the reviewed sha, base `main`, `mergeable_state: clean`, draft, no assignees (correct under the relay rule).
- Body r1 matches the code at every point I checked: the seven exports, the alias list, the case rule and its reasons, the `undefined` cases, the 59-case breakdown, the ledgers, the changeset. Its Verification block is honest about heads: the 102 derived gates ran at 8810e33cc and the scoped re-checks (spec test + typecheck, `check:generated` 14/14) at a8e812094; that is AGENTS.md rule 10's shape (full suite once before opening, scoped re-checks after).
- Comment 6622343873 on the PR is the contract-review claim for this head, not a dev report; the os-dev-report rule (.claude/agents/os-dev.md:62) names it as a pr_create write, so none is owed per push.
- Customer-facing text: the new docs and TSDoc carry no issue id in a served string; the mdx names "later phases" without an id, which matches the page's style elsewhere.

### ④ Design judgment

- Should-fix (mdx referent): the new paragraph attributes the key-order answer to "the fallback ladder below", but the page's `Locale Fallback` section lists only exact → language-only → declared default; it names neither the case step nor variant expansion, and the page never names `resolveBundleLocale`. A reader of the page alone cannot see which step turns `zh` into `zh-Hant`. One phrase fixes it: name `resolveBundleLocale` (`system/i18n-resolver.ts`, which the Display Label Forms table already cites) in that sentence, or add "else the first registered variant" to the ladder. The TSDoc already does this; the page does not.
- The transitional follow rule is the right call for phase 1 (ruling F's "every language" is unobeyable on metadata and emails today); the Callout keeps the gap visible on the served page rather than in a code comment, so the backfill phases inherit a page that contradicts nothing.
- Nothing new is introduced beyond the asked fixes: the delta touches no runtime path, adds no reader of the table, and the alias record's literal typing leaves `platformLocaleTagOf` as the only door that takes an arbitrary string.

## 维护者速读

- **改了什么：** `@objectstack/spec/system` 新导出平台语言表 `PLATFORM_LOCALES`（11 种语言，行 `{ tag, label, rtl }`，按菜单顺序，冻结），以及旧代码的读别名表 `PLATFORM_LOCALE_READ_ALIASES`（按十个字面量键定类型）和查询函数 `platformLocaleTagOf(code)`；i18n 协议文档补上这张表、别名和规则，并写明这张表是各界面要补齐的目标，今天实际只供给 Console 10 个语言包、元数据和邮件各 4 种语言。
- **为什么改：** 裁决 F（#29349）定下平台只认一张 11 种语言的表、无分级；这是 #29428 的第一步，后续 Console、元数据、邮件、语言菜单都从这张表读。
- **风险与回滚：** 低。纯新增导出，目前没有任何读取方，也不拒收任何非表内语言码，现有数据全部照旧解析。回滚即还原本 PR。
- **先看：** `packages/spec/src/system/platform-locales.ts`（表、别名、大小写不敏感的查询）；`packages/spec/src/system/platform-locales.test.ts`（整表与逐条别名的钉）。
- **两分钟验证：** `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec exec vitest run src/system/platform-locales.test.ts`，预期 `59 passed`。
- **需要你做的：** 无，席位落地。

席位意见：fable 契约复审两轮。首轮 FAIL，原因是文档把 11 种语言写成「今天已在所有界面齐全」。修正后 PASS，剩两处措辞级小问题，不值得再开一轮（见下）。check-runs 全绿，不在受管路径上，按普通队列落地。

## 席位核对 — ACCEPT · domain:spec#3 · head `a8e812094c6d07538541f1e6f734276516672223`

- **Shape:** 7 files, +353 −0, in three commits on `origin/main` `f19fbb8f`. The PR adds:
  - one new module, `packages/spec/src/system/platform-locales.ts`, holding the table (11 rows, deep-frozen, `rtl` only on `ar`), the tag list, the read-alias map typed on its ten literal keys, and the case-insensitive `platformLocaleTagOf`;
  - its barrel export and its test (59 cases);
  - the two ledgers an export moves (api-surface, export-origins);
  - the changeset;
  - an `i18n-standard.mdx` section.
- **Premise measured:** at `f19fbb8f`, `PLATFORM_LOCALES` did not exist, and locale codes were spelled inline. The review verified the new docs text against main: the Console has 10 packs with no `zh-Hant`, metadata has `en`/`zh-CN`/`ja-JP`/`es-ES` in all 10 `translations/` packages, and the emails have 4 locales with `EMAIL_TEMPLATE_FLOOR_LOCALE = 'en-US'`.
- **Gates (check-runs at this head):** 69 check-runs, 59 success, 10 skipped (path-filtered or opt-in), 0 red. The body guards reran after the body refresh and passed. Dev runs at this head: spec test and typecheck exit 0. The derived-gate sweep (102 of 102, all exit 0) ran at `8810e33c`. The two commits after it change only the TSDoc, the mdx, the alias typing and the two ledgers, and CI covers them at this head.
- **Contract review:**
  - Round 0, 6621942673 on `8810e33c`: FAIL. The must-fix was the docs stating the target as a present fact. The should-fixes were the ladder sentence, the Skills-docs `en-GB` claim and the alias typing.
  - Delta, 6622424793 on this head: PASS.
- **Declarations:** `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, `Metadata-protocol: none` (no schema reads the table, and nothing is refused or newly accepted), `@objectstack/spec: patch`, confirmed by `check-changeset-no-major`. ADR-0087 is not needed.
- **Accepted deviations:**
  - The derived-gate sweep is from the head before the fix round, as stated above.
  - Two wording nits from the delta review are not worth a round:
    - the mdx says "the fallback ladder below", while the page's Locale Fallback section does not list `resolveBundleLocale`'s variant-expansion step;
    - the body said "four value exports" for three. The seat corrected that in the body refresh.
  - The prior review's point about the PR having no assignee is overruled: os-dev PRs from a relay `pr_create` carry no assignee by rule.
- **Carried:** phases 2 to 4 of #29428 (the Console packs including `zh-Hant`, metadata and email backfill, and the locale menu) are later cards in their own lanes. The `Skills-docs:` line names the skills spellings owed while the skills lane is paused. The mdx ladder sentence can be tightened in phase 2, when `ui/packages/i18n` first reads the table.
- **Landing:** not governed (`check-governed-merges --pr 30007`: 0 of 7 paths, 353 lines). The hand-off is `pr_ready` plus `automerge_enable`, through the merge queue.
